subject: Banking
title: Real-Time Payment Networks
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Real-Time Payment Networks.

hook.text: FedNow launched in 2023 giving Americans instant bank-to-bank transfers 24/7. No more waiting for business hours.

buildup.text: Most countries already had real-time systems. The UK launched Faster Payments in 2008. The US was 15 years behind.

discovery.text: Real-time payments eliminate float, clearing delays, and business-hour restrictions. Money moves in seconds, any time.

twist.text: Instant payments enable instant fraud. Scammers love irrevocable transfers because victims cannot recall the money.

climax.text: Speed is a double-edged sword. Faster payments help everyone, including criminals. Security must match velocity.

punchline.text: Money moves in seconds, 24/7. So does fraud. Speed cuts both ways.

quiz.question: What is a major risk of real-time payment systems?
options: Instant irrevocable transfers make fraud harder to reverse

details.summary: Real-time payment networks like FedNow, UPI, and Pix settle bank-to-bank transfers in seconds rather than days, operating 24/7 and transforming expectations about how fast money should move between accounts.
details.whyItMatters: Real-time payments make the multi-day ACH clearing process obsolete for many use cases. Countries that have adopted them see dramatic improvements in financial inclusion and business cash flow.
takeaways: FedNow launched in 2023 as the US real-time payment system
India's UPI processes over 10 billion transactions monthly
Brazil's Pix reached 150 million users within two years of launch

faq.question: Why did the US take so long to build a real-time payment system?
faq.answer: Established card networks and ACH lobbied against disruption, banks were reluctant to invest in infrastructure that might reduce fee revenue, and regulatory fragmentation across state and federal levels slowed consensus.

faq.question: Do real-time payments increase fraud risk?
faq.answer: Yes. Instant irrevocable settlement means fraudulent transactions cannot be reversed as easily. Criminals exploit the speed to move stolen funds before detection. Real-time fraud monitoring must match real-time payment speed.
